description_full: Capstone Copper Corp., a copper mining company, mines, explores for, and develops mineral properties in the United States, Chile, and Mexico. The company primarily explores copper, silver, gold, molybdenum, zinc, iron, cobalt, and other base metals. Capstone Copper Corp. is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

financial_summary: CAPSTONE COPPER CORP. is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $5.8B market cap on $2.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +22% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 3% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 15% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $166M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.17× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.1× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 4.2×.

Net dilution runs at 0.2% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 8.1% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $1.33 (margin of safety -469%), so there is no valuation cushion.

prof: ROIC of 3% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.6%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.94).
It runs a 15% gross margin and converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 2.17x.
ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.1x equity multiplier).
SG&A jumped 14% last year, worth watching.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.1x net debt to EBITDA ($304.2M of cash against $1.3B of debt), with interest covered 4.2x.

growth: Revenue has compounded at 22.1% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 99% of profits supports about 2.6% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
own: Insiders own 8.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 41%.
Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-0.2%), diluting holders.
